A churning storm cloud forms for the duration, centered on a point within range and spreading to a radius of 300 feet. Each creature under the cloud when it appears must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 Thunder damage and have the Deafened condition for the duration.

At the start of each of your later turns, the storm produces different effects, as detailed below.

Turn 2. Acidic rain falls. Each creature and object under the cloud takes 4d6 Acid damage.

Turn 3. You call six bolts of lightning from the cloud to strike six different creatures or objects beneath it. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Turn 4. Hailstones rain down. Each creature under the cloud takes 2d6 Bludgeoning damage.

Turns 5-10. Gusts and freezing rain assail the area under the cloud. Each creature there takes 1d6 Cold damage. Until the spell ends, the area is Difficult Terrain and Heavily Obscured, ranged attacks with weapons are impossible there, and strong wind blows through the area.

storm sphere.name: Storm Sphere
storm sphere.summary: A 20-foot-radius storm is difficult terrain; creatures ending turns inside make a Str save for 2d6 bludgeoning. As a bonus action, a bolt from it hits for 4d6 lightning.
storm sphere.text: A 20-foot-radius ball of churning wind appears; its area is difficult terrain. A creature that enters it for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Strength save or takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage. As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can shoot lightning from its center at a creature within 60 feet with a ranged spell attack (advantage if the target is inside the sphere), dealing 4d6 lightning on a hit. Creatures within 30 feet of the sphere have disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on hearing.
storm sphere.higher: Both damage amounts increase by 1d6 per slot level above 4th.

suggestion.name: Suggestion
suggestion.summary: Suggest a reasonable-sounding course of action. Wis save or the target pursues it as best it can.
suggestion.text:
You suggest a course of activity-described in no more than 25 words-to one creature you can see within range that can hear and understand you. The suggestion must sound achievable and not involve anything that would obviously deal damage to the target or its allies. For example, you could say, "Fetch the key to the cult's treasure vault, and give the key to me." Or you could say, "Stop fighting, leave this library peacefully, and don't return."

The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed condition for the duration or until you or your allies deal damage to the target. The Charmed target pursues the suggestion to the best of its ability. The suggested activity can continue for the entire duration, but if the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the spell ends for the target upon completing it.

summon aberration.name: Summon Aberration
summon aberration.material: a pickled tentacle and an eyeball in a platinum-inlaid vial worth at least 400 gp
summon aberration.summary: Call an aberrant spirit (Beholderkin, Slaad or Star Spawn) that blasts, claws or slams with psychic power.
summon aberration.text: An aberrant spirit appears as a Beholderkin (flying, a 150-foot psychic eye ray), a Slaad (regenerates, claws that stop healing) or a Star Spawn (a psychic slam and an aura that deals psychic damage to nearby foes). It has AC 11 + the spell's level and 40 hit points plus 10 per slot level above 4th, and attacks a number of times equal to half the spell's level, each dealing about 1d8 or 1d10 + 3 + the spell's level. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon aberration.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon beast.name: Summon Beast
summon beast.material: a feather, tuft of fur and fish tail inside a gilded acorn worth at least 200 gp
summon beast.summary: Call a bestial spirit in air, land or water form that fights for you with a maul-like bite and scaling stats.
summon beast.text: A bestial spirit appears in your chosen form: Air (flying, can fly past foes without opportunity attacks), Land (climbs, pack tactics) or Water (swims, breathes water, pack tactics). It has AC 11 + the spell's level, 20 (Air) or 30 (Land, Water) hit points plus 5 per slot level above 2nd, and makes a number of attacks equal to half the spell's level, each dealing 1d8 + 4 + the spell's level piercing. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon beast.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon celestial.name: Summon Celestial
summon celestial.material: a golden reliquary worth at least 500 gp
summon celestial.summary: Call a flying celestial spirit, an Avenger with a radiant bow or a Defender with a radiant mace, that can also heal once.
summon celestial.text: A celestial spirit appears as an Avenger (a radiant bow attack) or a Defender (a radiant mace that grants an ally temporary hit points, and +2 AC). It has AC 11 + the spell's level, 40 hit points plus 10 per slot level above 5th, a flying speed, and attacks a number of times equal to half the spell's level. Once per casting it can touch a creature to heal 2d8 + the spell's level hit points. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon celestial.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon construct.name: Summon Construct
summon construct.material: an ornate stone and metal lockbox worth at least 400 gp
summon construct.summary: Call a construct spirit of clay, metal or stone that slams foes and punishes those who strike it.
summon construct.text: A construct spirit appears made of Clay (lashes out when it's hit), Metal (burns creatures that hit it in melee) or Stone (sluggishness for creatures that start their turns near it). It has AC 13 + the spell's level, 40 hit points plus 15 per slot level above 4th, and makes a number of slams equal to half the spell's level, each dealing 1d8 + 4 + the spell's level bludgeoning. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon construct.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon dragon.name: Summon Dragon
summon dragon.material: an object with the image of a, dragon engraved on it worth 500+ GP
summon dragon.summary: You call forth a Dragon spirit.
summon dragon.text:
You call forth a Dragon spirit. It manifests in an unoccupied space that you can see within range and uses the Draconic Spirit stat block. The creature disappears when it drops to 0 Hit Points or when the spell ends.

The creature is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your Initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.
summon dragon.higher: Use the spell slot's level for the spell's level in the stat block. Large Dragon, Neutral AC 14 + the spell's level HP 50 + 10 for each spell level above 5 Speed 30 ft., Fly 60 ft., Swim 30 ft. MOD SAVE    MOD SAVE    MOD SAVE Str 19 +4 +4 dex 14 +2 +2 con 17 +3 +3 int  10 +0 +0 WiS 14 +2 +2 chA 14 +2 +2 Resistances Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison Immunities Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned Senses Blindsight 30 ft., Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 12 Languages Draconic, understands the languages you know CR None (XP 0; PB equals your Proficiency Bonus) Traits     Shared Resistances. When you summon the spirit, choose one of its Resistances. You have Resistance to the chosen damage type until the spell ends. Actions     Multiattack. The spirit makes a number of Rend attacks equal to half the spell's level (round down), and it uses Breath Weapon. Rend. Melee Attack Roll: Bonus equals your spell attack modifier, reach 10 feet. Hit: 1d6 + 4 + the spell's level Piercing damage. Breath Weapon. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC equals your spell save DC, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. Failure: 2d6 damage of a type this spirit has Resistance to (your choice when you cast the spell). Success: Half damage.

summon elemental.name: Summon Elemental
summon elemental.material: air, a pebble, ash and water inside a gold-inlaid vial worth at least 400 gp
summon elemental.summary: Call an air, earth, fire or water elemental spirit that slams foes and resists or ignores matching damage.
summon elemental.text: An elemental spirit of Air (flies fast), Earth (moves through earth and stone), Fire (fire damage, sheds light) or Water (swims) appears. It has AC 11 + the spell's level, 50 hit points plus 10 per slot level above 4th, can squeeze through tight spaces, and makes a number of slams equal to half the spell's level, each dealing 1d10 + 4 + the spell's level (bludgeoning, or fire for the Fire form). It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon elemental.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon fey.name: Summon Fey
summon fey.material: a gilded flower worth at least 300 gp
summon fey.summary: Call a fey spirit (Fuming, Mirthful or Tricksy) that strikes with a magic shortsword and teleports with a bonus effect.
summon fey.text: A fey spirit appears in the mood you choose. It has AC 12 + the spell's level, 30 hit points plus 10 per slot level above 3rd, and makes a number of shortsword attacks equal to half the spell's level, each dealing 1d6 + 3 + the spell's level piercing plus 1d6 force. As a bonus action it can teleport 30 feet and gain a mood effect: Fuming gives advantage on its next attack, Mirthful can charm a nearby creature, Tricksy fills a space it left with magical darkness. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon fey.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon fiend.name: Summon Fiend
summon fiend.material: humanoid blood inside a ruby vial worth at least 600 gp
summon fiend.summary: Call a fiendish spirit, a Demon, Devil or Yugoloth, that bites, burns or claws your foes.
summon fiend.text: A fiendish spirit appears as a Demon (a necrotic bite; explodes when it dies), a Devil (flies, a fiery strike, sees through magical darkness) or a Yugoloth (claws, can teleport after attacking). It has AC 12 + the spell's level and 50 (Demon), 40 (Devil) or 60 (Yugoloth) hit points plus 15 per slot level above 6th, resists fire, and attacks a number of times equal to half the spell's level. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon fiend.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon greater demon.name: Summon Greater Demon
summon greater demon.material: a vial of blood from a humanoid killed within the past 24 hours
summon greater demon.summary: Summon a demon of CR 5 or lower that obeys you until it succeeds on a Charisma save at the end of one of its turns.
summon greater demon.text: You summon a demon of your choice with a challenge rating of 5 or lower. It acts on your initiative and follows your spoken commands. At the end of each of its turns it makes a Charisma save (with disadvantage if you speak its true name); on a success your control ends and it attacks the nearest non-demons. You may draw a protective blood circle when casting that the demon can't cross or affect. If you lose concentration early, an uncontrolled demon lingers for 1d6 rounds before vanishing.
summon greater demon.higher: The maximum challenge rating rises by 1 per slot level above 4th.

summon lesser demons.name: Summon Lesser Demons
summon lesser demons.material: a vial of blood from a humanoid killed within the past 24 hours
summon lesser demons.summary: Summon a random group of weak demons (2 of CR 1, 4 of CR 1/2 or 8 of CR 1/4) that attack the nearest non-demons.
summon lesser demons.text: Roll a d6: on 1-2 two demons of challenge rating 1 or lower appear, on 3-4 four of CR 1/2 or lower, on 5-6 eight of CR 1/4 or lower (the DM picks them). They are hostile to all non-demons, act as a group on their own initiative, and attack the nearest non-demons. You may use the blood to draw a protective circle when casting; while it lasts the demons can't cross it or harm anyone inside. The demons vanish at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon lesser demons.higher: With a 6th- or 7th-level slot, twice as many demons appear; with an 8th- or 9th-level slot, three times as many.

summon shadowspawn.name: Summon Shadowspawn
summon shadowspawn.material: tears inside a gem worth at least 300 gp
summon shadowspawn.summary: Call a shadow spirit (Fury, Despair or Fear) whose chilling claws deal cold damage and whose scream frightens foes.
summon shadowspawn.text: A shadowy spirit appears in the form of Fury (advantage on attacks against frightened creatures), Despair (slows creatures near it) or Fear (can vanish into dim light or darkness). It has AC 11 + the spell's level, 35 hit points plus 15 per slot level above 3rd, and makes a number of attacks equal to half the spell's level, each dealing 1d12 + 3 + the spell's level cold. Once per casting it can shriek, forcing creatures within 30 feet to make a Wisdom save or be frightened for 1 minute. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon shadowspawn.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

summon undead.name: Summon Undead
summon undead.material: a gilded skull worth at least 300 gp
summon undead.summary: Call an undead spirit (Ghostly, Putrid or Skeletal) that frightens, paralyzes or shoots necrotic bolts.
summon undead.text: An undead spirit appears as Ghostly (flies through objects; its touch deals necrotic damage and can frighten), Putrid (a festering aura that poisons; its claws can paralyze poisoned foes) or Skeletal (a ranged grave bolt dealing necrotic damage). It has AC 11 + the spell's level and 30 hit points plus 10 per slot level above 3rd (Skeletal has 20), and attacks a number of times equal to half the spell's level, each dealing roughly 1d8 + 3 + the spell's level. It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls initiative with you and acts right after you, obeys your spoken commands (taking the Dodge action if given none), and vanishes at 0 hit points or when the spell ends.
summon undead.higher: Use the slot level wherever the spell's level appears in the creature's statistics, making it tougher and adding attacks at higher levels.

sunbeam.name: Sunbeam
sunbeam.summary: A beam of brilliant light flashes out from your hand in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long line.
sunbeam.text:
You launch a sunbeam in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long Line. Each creature in the Line makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 Radiant damage and has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

Until the spell ends, you can take a Magic action to create a new Line of radiance.

For the duration, a mote of brilliant radiance shines above you. It sheds Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. This light is sunlight.

sunburst.name: Sunburst
sunburst.summary: Brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you choose within range.
sunburst.text:
Brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in the Sphere makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 12d6 Radiant damage and has the Blinded condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

A creature Blinded by this spell makes another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

This spell dispels Darkness in its area that was created by any spell.

swift quiver.name: Swift Quiver
swift quiver.material: a quiver holding at least one piece of ammunition
swift quiver.summary: A quiver never runs dry, and each turn you can use a bonus action to make two attacks with a weapon using its ammo.
swift quiver.text: The quiver you touch produces an endless supply of nonmagical ammunition. On each of your turns until the spell ends, you can use a bonus action to make two attacks with a weapon that draws ammunition from it. Each piece of conjured ammunition crumbles to dust once it hits or misses.

sword burst.name: Sword Burst
sword burst.summary: A ring of spectral blades: each creature within 5 ft makes a Dex save or takes 1d6 force.
sword burst.text: Phantom blades sweep around you. Each creature within 5 feet of you, other than you, makes a Dexterity save or takes 1d6 force damage.
sword burst.higher: Damage rises by one die at 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

symbol.name: Symbol
symbol.material: powdered diamond worth 1,000+ GP, which the spell consumes
symbol.summary: When you cast this spell, you inscribe a harmful glyph either on a surface (such as a section of floor, a wall, or a table) or within an object that can be closed to conceal the glyph (such as a...
symbol.text:
You inscribe a harmful glyph either on a surface (such as a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book or chest). The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If you choose an object, it must remain in place; if it is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly imperceptible and requires a successful Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC to notice.

When you inscribe the glyph, you set its trigger and choose which effect the symbol bears: Death, Discord, Fear, Pain, Sleep, or Stunning. Each one is explained below.

Set the Trigger. You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, common triggers include touching or stepping on the glyph, removing another object covering it, or approaching within a certain distance of it. For glyphs inscribed within an object, common triggers include opening that object or seeing the glyph.

You can refine the trigger so that only creatures of certain types activate it (for example, the glyph could be set to affect Aberrations). You can also set conditions for creatures that don't trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

Once triggered, the glyph glows, filling a 60-foot-radius Sphere with Dim Light for 10 minutes, after which time the spell ends. Each creature in the Sphere when the glyph activates is targeted by its effect, as is a creature that enters the Sphere for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. A creature is targeted only once per turn.

Death. Each target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d10 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.

Discord. Each target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target argues with other creatures for 1 minute. During this time, it is incapable of meaningful communication and has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

Fear. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. While Frightened, the target must move at least 30 feet away from the glyph on each of its turns, if able.

Pain. Each target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition for 1 minute.

Sleep. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Unconscious condition for 10 minutes. A creature awakens if it takes damage or if someone takes an action to shake it awake.

Stunning. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Stunned condition for 1 minute.

synaptic static.name: Synaptic Static
synaptic static.summary: A 20-ft psychic burst: Int save or 8d6 psychic and -1d6 on attacks, checks and concentration saves for a minute; half on a save.
synaptic static.text: Psychic energy explodes in a 20-foot-radius sphere at a point you choose. Each creature there makes an Intelligence save (creatures with Intelligence 2 or lower are unaffected), taking 8d6 psychic damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature that fails also has muddled thoughts for 1 minute: it subtracts 1d6 from attack rolls, ability checks and Constitution saves to maintain concentration, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns to end this.

tasha's caustic brew.name: Tasha's Caustic Brew
tasha's caustic brew.summary: A 30-ft line of acid: Dex save or coated, taking 2d4 acid at the start of each turn until scraped off.
tasha's caustic brew.text: A stream of acid sprays from you in a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the line makes a Dexterity save or is coated in acid until the spell ends or someone uses an action to scrape or wash it off. A coated creature takes 2d4 acid damage at the start of each of its turns.

tasha's mind whip.name: Tasha's Mind Whip
tasha's mind whip.summary: Int save or 3d6 psychic, no reactions, and on its next turn only one of move, action or bonus action; half and nothing else on a save.
tasha's mind whip.text: You lash a creature's mind; it makes an Intelligence save. On a failure it takes 3d6 psychic damage, can't take reactions until the end of its next turn, and on that turn can use only one of its movement, action or bonus action. On a success it takes half damage and suffers nothing else.
tasha's mind whip.higher: One additional creature per slot level above 2nd, each within 30 feet of another.

tasha's otherworldly guise.name: Tasha's Otherworldly Guise
tasha's otherworldly guise.material: an object engraved with a symbol of the Outer Planes, worth at least 500 gp
tasha's otherworldly guise.summary: Take on an Upper or Lower Planes aspect: two immunities, wings with 40-ft flight, +2 AC, and two magical attacks using your casting stat.
tasha's otherworldly guise.text: You draw on the Upper Planes (immunity to radiant and necrotic damage and to being charmed) or the Lower Planes (immunity to fire and poison damage and to being poisoned). You sprout wings and gain a flying speed of 40 feet, gain +2 AC, your weapon attacks count as magical and can use your spellcasting modifier for attack and damage rolls, and you attack twice when you take the Attack action (this doesn't stack with Extra Attack).

telekinesis.name: Telekinesis
telekinesis.summary: Move a Huge or smaller creature (it contests with Strength) or an object up to 1,000 pounds up to 30 feet each turn, holding it in place if you like.
telekinesis.text:
You gain the ability to move or manipulate creatures or objects by thought. When you cast the spell and as a Magic action on your later turns before the spell ends, you can exert your will on one creature or object that you can see within range, causing the appropriate effect below. You can affect the same target round after round or choose a new one at any time. If you switch targets, the prior target is no longer affected by the spell.

Creature. You can try to move a Huge or smaller creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range. Until the end of your next turn, the creature has the Restrained condition, and if you lift it into the air, it is suspended there. It falls at the end of your next turn unless you use this option on it again and it fails the save.

Object. You can try to move a Huge or smaller object. If the object isn't being worn or carried, you automatically move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

If the object is worn or carried by a creature, that creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or you pull the object away and move it up to 30 feet in any direction within the spell's range.

You can exert fine control on objects with your telekinetic grip, such as manipulating a simple tool,

telepathic bond.name: Telepathic Bond
telepathic bond.summary: You forge a telepathic link among up to eight willing creatures of your choice within range, psychically linking each creature to all the others for the duration.
telepathic bond.text:
You forge a telepathic link among up to eight willing creatures of your choice within range, psychically linking each creature to all the others for the duration. Creatures that can't communicate in any languages aren't affected by this spell.

Until the spell ends, the targets can communicate telepathically through the bond whether or not they share a language. The communication is possible over any distance, though it can't extend to other planes of existence.

telepathy.name: Telepathy
telepathy.material: a pair of linked silver rings
telepathy.summary: Link minds with a familiar willing creature anywhere on your plane to share words, images and sensations for 24 hours.
telepathy.text: You create a telepathic connection with a willing creature you are familiar with that is on the same plane as you. For the duration you can instantly exchange words, images, sounds and other sensory messages, and the creature understands you even without a shared language. The creature needs an Intelligence of at least 1 for the link to work.

teleport.name: Teleport
teleport.summary: This spell instantly transports you and up to eight willing creatures of your choice that you can see within range, or a single object that you can see within range, to a destination you select.
teleport.text:
This spell instantly transports you and up to eight willing creatures that you can see within range, or a single object that you can see within range, to a destination you select. If you target an object, it must be Large or smaller, and it can't be held or carried by an unwilling creature.

The destination you choose must be known to you, and it must be on the same plane of existence as you. Your familiarity with the destination determines whether you arrive there successfully. The GM rolls 1d100 and consults the Teleportation Outcome table and the explanations after it. Teleportation  Outcome Familiarity Mishap Similar Area  Off Target

On Target Permanent circle 01-00 Linked object 01-00 Very familiar 01-05 06-13 14-24 25-00 Seen casually 01-33 34-43 44-53 54-00 Viewed once or described 01-43 44-53 54-73 74-00 False destination 01-50 51-00 -

Familiarity. Here are the meanings of the terms in the table's Familiarity column: • "Permanent circle" means a permanent teleportation circle whose sigil sequence you know. • "Linked object" means you possess an object taken from the desired destination within the last six months, such as a book from a wizard's library. • "Very familiar" is a place you have visited often, a place you have carefully studied, or a place you can see when you cast the spell. • "Seen casually" is a place you have seen more than once but with which you aren't very familiar. • "Viewed once or described" is a place you have seen once, possibly using magic, or a place you know through someone else's description, perhaps from a map. • "False destination" is a place that doesn't exist. Perhaps you tried to scry an enemy's sanctum but instead viewed an illusion, or you are attempting to teleport to a location that no longer exists.

Mishap. The spell's unpredictable magic results in a difficult journey. Each teleporting creature (or the target object) takes 3d10 Force damage, and the GM rerolls on the table to see where you wind up (multiple mishaps can occur, dealing damage each time).

Similar Area. You and your group (or the target object) appear in a different area that's visually or thematically similar to the target area. You appear in the closest similar place. If you are heading for your home laboratory, for example, you might appear in another person's laboratory in the same city.

Off Target. You and your group (or the target object) appear 2d12 miles away from the destination in a random direction. Roll 1d8 for the direction: 1, east; 2, southeast; 3, south; 4, southwest; 5, west; 6, northwest; 7, north; or 8, northeast.

On Target. You and your group (or the target object) appear where you intended.

teleportation circle.name: Teleportation Circle
teleportation circle.material: rare inks worth 50+ GP, which the, spell consumes
teleportation circle.summary: Draw a circle linked to a permanent circle whose sigils you know. Anyone entering it appears at that destination.
teleportation circle.text:
As you cast the spell, you draw a 5-foot-radius circle on the ground inscribed with sigils that link your location to a permanent teleportation circle of your choice whose sigil sequence you know and that is on the same plane of existence as you. A shimmering portal opens within the circle you drew and remains open until the end of your next turn. Any creature that enters the portal instantly appears within 5 feet of the destination circle or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.

Many major temples, guildhalls, and other important places have permanent teleportation circles. Each circle includes a unique sigil sequence-a string of runes arranged in a particular pattern.

When you first gain the ability to cast this spell, you learn the sigil sequences for two destinations on the Material Plane, determined by the GM. You might learn additional sigil sequences during your adventures. You can commit a new sigil sequence to memory after studying it for 1 minute.

You can create a permanent teleportation circle by casting this spell in the same location every day for 365 days.

temple of the gods.name: Temple of the Gods
temple of the gods.material: a holy symbol worth at least 5 gp
temple of the gods.summary: Raise a temple up to a 120-ft cube that repels chosen creature types, blocks divination, and boosts healing inside.
temple of the gods.text: A temple of your deity's style appears on the ground, up to a 120-foot cube, with a floor, walls, doors and a roof. Choose celestials, elementals, fey, fiends or undead: such creatures must make a Charisma save to enter, and even those that get in subtract 1d4 from attack rolls, ability checks and saves inside. Divination magic can't perceive inside the temple, and anyone healed there by a spell of 1st level or higher regains extra hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Casting it in the same spot every day for a year makes it permanent.

tenser's transformation.name: Tenser's Transformation
tenser's transformation.material: a few hairs from a bull
tenser's transformation.summary: Become a warrior: 50 temp HP, weapon proficiencies, advantage on weapon attacks, +2d12 force, an extra attack; no spellcasting.
tenser's transformation.text: You gain 50 temporary hit points, proficiency with all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons and with Strength and Constitution saves, advantage on weapon attack rolls, an extra 2d12 force damage on weapon hits, and you attack twice when you take the Attack action. You can't cast spells while transformed. When the spell ends you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or gain a level of exhaustion.

thaumaturgy.name: Thaumaturgy
thaumaturgy.summary: You manifest a minor wonder, a sign of supernatural power, within range.
thaumaturgy.text:
You manifest a minor wonder within range. You create one of the effects below within range. If you cast this spell multiple times, you can have up to three of its 1-minute effects active at a time.

Altered Eyes. You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.

Booming Voice. Your voice booms up to three times as loud as normal for 1 minute. For the duration, you have Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks.

Fire Play. You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change color for 1 minute.

Invisible Hand. You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.

Phantom Sound. You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point of your choice within range, such as a rumble of thunder, the cry of a raven, or ominous whispers.

Tremors. You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.

thorn whip.name: Thorn Whip
thorn whip.material: the stem of a plant with thorns
thorn whip.summary: Melee spell attack at up to 30 ft for 1d6 piercing; a Large or smaller target is pulled up to 10 feet toward you.
thorn whip.text: A thorny vine lashes out at a creature within range; make a melee spell attack. On a hit the target takes 1d6 piercing damage, and if it is Large or smaller you can pull it up to 10 feet closer to you.
thorn whip.higher: Damage rises by one die at 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

thunder step.name: Thunder Step
thunder step.summary: You teleport, optionally taking an adjacent willing ally. Creatures within 10 feet of where you left make a Con save for 3d10 thunder, half on a success.
thunder step.text: You teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within range. Each creature within 10 feet of the space you left makes a Constitution save, taking 3d10 thunder damage on a failure or half on a success; the boom is audible 300 feet away. You can bring one willing creature your size or smaller that is within 5 feet of you; it appears within 5 feet of your destination.

thunderclap.name: Thunderclap
thunderclap.summary: Each other creature within 5 ft makes a Con save or takes 1d6 thunder; the boom is audible 100 feet away.
thunderclap.text: You make a burst of thunderous sound heard up to 100 feet away. Every creature within 5 feet of you other than yourself makes a Constitution save or takes 1d6 thunder damage.
thunderclap.higher: Damage rises by one die at 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

thunderous smite.name: Thunderous Smite
thunderous smite.summary: Next melee weapon hit deals +2d6 thunder; Str save or the target is pushed 10 feet and knocked prone.
thunderous smite.text: The first time you hit with a melee weapon attack during the duration, the weapon booms with a thunderclap heard 300 feet away and the attack deals an extra 2d6 thunder damage. If the target is a creature, it makes a Strength save or is pushed 10 feet away from you and knocked prone.

thunderwave.name: Thunderwave
thunderwave.summary: A thunderous wave: Con save or take 2d8 thunder damage and be pushed 10 feet; half and no push on a success. Audible 300 feet away.
thunderwave.text:
You unleash a wave of thunderous energy. Each creature in a 15-foot Cube originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 Thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

In addition, unsecured objects that are entirely within the Cube are pushed 10 feet away from you, and a thunderous boom is audible within 300 feet.
thunderwave.higher: The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

tidal wave.name: Tidal Wave
tidal wave.summary: A wave 30 feet long, 10 feet wide and 10 feet tall crashes down: Dex save or take 4d8 bludgeoning and fall prone, half and no prone on a success.
tidal wave.text: A wave up to 30 feet long, 10 feet wide and 10 feet tall appears at a point you choose. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save, taking 4d8 bludgeoning damage and falling prone on a failure, or half damage without falling on a success. The water then spreads out, extinguishing unprotected flames in and within 30 feet of the area, before vanishing.

time stop.name: Time Stop
time stop.summary: You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself.
time stop.text:
You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. No time passes for other creatures, while you take 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, during which you can use actions and move as normal.

This spell ends if one of the actions you use during this period, or any effects that you create during it, affects a creature other than you or an object being worn or carried by someone other than you. In addition, the spell ends if you move to a place more than 1,000 feet from the location where you cast it.

tiny hut.name: Tiny Hut
tiny hut.summary: A dome shelters you and up to nine others, blocking outside creatures and spells and keeping the weather out. Can be cast as a ritual.
tiny hut.text:
A 10-foot Emanation springs into existence around you and remains stationary for the duration. The spell fails when you cast it if the Emanation isn't big enough to fully encapsulate all creatures in its area.

Creatures and objects within the Emanation when you cast the spell can move through it freely. All other creatures and objects are barred from passing through it. Spells of level 3 or lower can't be cast through it, and the effects of such spells can't extend into it.

The atmosphere inside the Emanation is comfortable and dry, regardless of the weather outside. Until the spell ends, you can command the interior to have Dim Light or Darkness (no action required). The Emanation is opaque from the outside and of any color you choose, but it's transparent from the inside.

The spell ends early if you leave the Emanation or if you cast it again.

tiny servant.name: Tiny Servant
tiny servant.summary: A Tiny unattended object grows arms and legs and serves you as a small creature you command with a bonus action.
tiny servant.text: You animate a Tiny nonmagical object no one is wearing or carrying, which becomes a tiny servant creature (AC 15, 10 hit points, 30-foot walk and climb speeds, a 1d4 + 3 bludgeoning slam). It is friendly to you and obeys mental commands you issue as a bonus action while it is within 120 feet; otherwise it defends itself. It reverts to an object if it drops to 0 hit points.
tiny servant.higher: Two more objects per slot level above 3rd.

toll the dead.name: Toll the Dead
toll the dead.summary: Wis save or 1d8 necrotic, or 1d12 necrotic if the target is already missing any hit points.
toll the dead.text: A mournful bell tolls around a creature you can see, which makes a Wisdom save. On a failure it takes 1d8 necrotic damage, or 1d12 necrotic damage if it was missing any hit points.
toll the dead.higher: Damage dice increase by one at 5th level (2d8 or 2d12), 11th level (3d8 or 3d12) and 17th level (4d8 or 4d12).

tongues.name: Tongues
tongues.summary: A creature understands any spoken language, and anyone who speaks a language understands it.
tongues.text: This spell grants the creature you touch the ability to understand any spoken or signed language that it hears or sees. Moreover, when the target communicates by speaking or signing, any creature that knows at least one language can understand it if that creature can hear the speech or see the signing.

transmute rock.name: Transmute Rock
transmute rock.summary: Turn up to a 40-ft cube of stone into deep mud that bogs creatures down, or turn mud into stone that can trap them.
transmute rock.text: Choose an area of stone or mud up to a 40-foot cube. Rock to mud: the stone becomes mud up to 10 feet deep that is very costly to move through, creatures standing on it may sink and be restrained (Strength save), and mud formed on a ceiling falls on creatures below (Dexterity save, 4d8 bludgeoning, half on a success). Mud to rock: mud or quicksand hardens into stone; creatures in it make a Dexterity save or become restrained in the rock, which can be broken free with a DC 20 Strength check or by destroying the surrounding stone.

transport via plants.name: Transport via Plants
transport via plants.summary: This spell creates a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within range and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence.
transport via plants.text: This spell creates a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within range and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence. You must have seen or touched the destination plant at least once before. For the duration, any creature can step into the target plant and exit from the destination plant by using 5 feet of movement.

tree stride.name: Tree Stride
tree stride.summary: You gain the ability to enter a tree and move from inside it to inside another tree of the same kind within 500 feet.
tree stride.text:
You gain the ability to enter a tree and move from inside it to inside another tree of the same kind within 500 feet. Both trees must be living and at least the same size as you. You must use 5 feet of movement to enter a tree. You instantly know the location of all other trees of the same kind within 500 feet and, as part of the move used to enter the tree, can either pass into one of those trees or step out of the tree you're in. You appear in a spot of your choice within 5 feet of the destination tree, using another 5 feet of movement. If you have no movement left, you appear within 5 feet of the tree you entered.

You can use this transportation ability only once on each of your turns. You must end each turn outside a tree.

true polymorph.name: True Polymorph
true polymorph.material: a drop of mercury, a dollop of gum arabic, and a wisp of smoke
true polymorph.summary: Choose one creature or nonmagical object that you can see within range.
true polymorph.text:
Choose one creature or nonmagical object that you can see within range. The creature shape-shifts into a different creature or a nonmagical object, or the object shape-shifts into a creature (the object must be neither worn nor carried). The transformation lasts for the duration or until the target dies or is destroyed, but if you maintain Concentration on this spell for the full duration, the spell lasts until dispelled.

An unwilling creature can make a Wisdom saving throw, and if it succeeds, it isn't affected by this spell.

Creature into Creature. If you turn a creature into another kind of creature, the new form can be any kind you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal to or less than the target's Challenge Rating or level. The target's game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the new form, but it retains its Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, alignment, and personality.

The target gains a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the Hit Points of the new form. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the spell ends.

The target is limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells.

The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

Object into Creature. You can turn an object into any kind of creature, as long as the creature's size is no larger than the object's size and the creature has a Challenge Rating of 9 or lower. The creature is Friendly to you and your allies. In combat, it takes its turns immediately after yours, and it obeys your commands.

If the spell lasts more than an hour, you no longer control the creature. It might remain Friendly to you, depending on how you have treated it.

Creature into Object. If you turn a creature into an object, it transforms along with whatever it is wearing and carrying into that form, as long as the object's size is no larger than the creature's size. The creature's statistics become those of the object, and the creature has no memory of time spent in this form after the spell ends and it returns to normal.

true resurrection.name: True Resurrection
true resurrection.material: diamonds worth 25,000+ GP,, which the spell consumes
true resurrection.summary: You touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that died for any reason except old age.
true resurrection.text:
You touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that died for any reason except old age. The creature is revived with all its Hit Points.

This spell closes all wounds, neutralizes any poison, cures all magical contagions, and lifts any curses affecting the creature when it died. The spell replaces damaged or missing organs and limbs. If the creature was Undead, it is restored to its non-Undead form.

The spell can provide a new body if the original no longer exists, in which case you must speak the creature's name. The creature then appears in an unoccupied space you choose within 10 feet of you.

true seeing.name: True Seeing
true seeing.material: mushroom powder worth 25+, GP, which the spell consumes
true seeing.summary: This spell gives the willing creature you touch the ability to see things as they actually are.
true seeing.text: For the duration, the willing creature you touch has Truesight with a range of 120 feet.

true strike.name: True Strike
true strike.material: a weapon with which you have proficiency and that is worth 1+ CP
true strike.summary: You extend your hand and point a finger at a target in range.
true strike.text: Guided by a flash of magical insight, you make one attack with the weapon used in the spell's casting. The attack uses your spellcasting ability for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity. If the attack deals damage, it can be Radiant damage or the weapon's normal damage type (your choice).
true strike.higher: Whether you deal Radiant damage or the weapon's normal damage type, the attack deals extra Radiant damage when you reach levels 5 (1d6), 11 (2d6), and 17 (3d6).

tsunami.name: Tsunami
tsunami.summary: A wall of water up to 300 ft long and high crashes forward 50 ft a round, dealing 6d10 then shrinking bludgeoning damage.
tsunami.text:
A wall of water springs into existence at a point you choose within range. You can make the wall up to 300 feet long, 300 feet high, and 50 feet thick. The wall lasts for the duration.

When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Strength saving throw, taking 6d10 Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

At the start of each of your turns after the wall appears, the wall, along with any creatures in it, moves 50 feet away from you. Any Huge or smaller creature inside the wall or whose space the wall enters when it moves must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 5d10 Bludgeoning damage. A creature can take this damage only once per round. At the end of the turn, the wall's height is reduced by 50 feet, and the damage the wall deals on later rounds is reduced by 1d10. When the wall reaches 0 feet in height, the spell ends.

A creature caught in the wall can move by swimming. Because of the wave's force, though, the creature must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC to move at all. If it fails the check, it can't move. A creature that moves out of the wall falls to the ground.

unseen servant.name: Unseen Servant
unseen servant.material: a bit of string and of wood
unseen servant.summary: This spell creates an invisible, mindless, shapeless force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends.
unseen servant.text:
This spell creates an Invisible, mindless, shapeless, Medium force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends. The servant springs into existence in an unoccupied space on the ground within range. It has AC 10, 1 Hit Point, and a Strength of 2, and it can't attack. If it drops to 0 Hit Points, the spell ends.

Once on each of your turns as a Bonus Action, you can mentally command the servant to move up to 15 feet and interact with an object. The servant can perform simple tasks that a human could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring drinks. Once you give the command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command.

If you command the servant to perform a task that would move it more than 60 feet away from you, the spell ends.

vampiric touch.name: Vampiric Touch
vampiric touch.summary: Make a melee spell attack for 3d6 necrotic damage and regain half the damage dealt. You can repeat the attack as an action each turn.
vampiric touch.text:
The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds. Make a melee spell attack against one creature within reach. On a hit, the target takes 3d6 Necrotic damage, and you regain Hit Points equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.

Until the spell ends, you can make the attack again on each of your turns as a Magic action, targeting the same creature or a different one.
vampiric touch.higher: The damage increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 3.

vicious mockery.name: Vicious Mockery
vicious mockery.summary: You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at a creature you can see within range.
vicious mockery.text: You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at one creature you can see or hear within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d6 Psychic damage and have Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.
vicious mockery.higher: The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6).

vitriolic sphere.name: Vitriolic Sphere
vitriolic sphere.summary: An acid ball bursts in a 20-ft radius: Dex save or 10d4 acid now and 5d4 at the end of its next turn; half and no lingering on a save.
vitriolic sphere.text: You point at a location within range, and a glowing, 1-foot-diameter ball of acid streaks there and explodes in a 20-foot-radius Sphere. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 10d4 Acid damage and another 5d4 Acid damage at the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half the initial damage only.
vitriolic sphere.higher: The initial damage increases by 2d4 for each spell slot level above 4.

wall of fire.name: Wall of Fire
wall of fire.summary: A wall of fire up to 60 feet long or a 20-foot ring: Dex save for 5d8 fire when it appears. One side burns creatures ending turns within 10 feet for 5d8 fire.
wall of fire.text:
You create a wall of fire on a solid surface within range. You can make the wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter, 20 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and lasts for the duration.

When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 5d8 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

One side of the wall, selected by you when you cast this spell, deals 5d8 Fire damage to each creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall. A creature takes the same damage when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there. The other side of the wall deals no damage.
wall of fire.higher: The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 4.

wall of force.name: Wall of Force
wall of force.summary: An invisible, indestructible wall, dome or sphere of force appears. Nothing physical can pass through it; disintegrate destroys it.
wall of force.text:
An Invisible wall of force springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall appears in any orientation you choose, as a horizontal or vertical barrier or at an angle. It can be free floating or resting on a solid surface. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-by-10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1/4 inch thick and lasts for the duration. If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side).

Nothing can physically pass through the wall. It is immune to all damage and can't be dispelled by Dispel Magic. A Disintegrate spell destroys the wall instantly, however. The wall also extends into the Ethereal Plane and blocks ethereal travel through the wall.

wall of ice.name: Wall of Ice
wall of ice.summary: You create a wall of ice on a solid surface within range.
wall of ice.text:
You create a wall of ice on a solid surface within range. You can form it into a hemispherical dome or a globe with a radius of up to 10 feet, or you can shape a flat surface made up of ten 10-foot-square panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. In any form, the wall is 1 foot thick and lasts for the duration.

If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side) and makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The wall is an object that can be damaged and thus breached. It has AC 12 and 30 Hit Points per 10-foot section, and it has Immunity to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage and Vulnerability to Fire damage. Reducing a 10-foot section of wall to 0 Hit Points destroys it and leaves behind a sheet of frigid air in the space the wall occupied.

A creature moving through the sheet of frigid air for the first time on a turn makes a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d6 Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
wall of ice.higher: The damage the wall deals when it appears increases by 2d6 and the damage from passing through the sheet of frigid air increases by 1d6 for each spell slot level above 6.

wall of light.name: Wall of Light
wall of light.summary: A 60-ft wall of light (Con save, 4d8 radiant and blinded) that you can shrink to fire 4d8 radiant beams at foes.
wall of light.text: A shimmering wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high and 5 feet thick appears, blocking sight but not movement and shedding bright light 120 feet and dim light another 120. Creatures in its area when it appears make a Constitution save, taking 4d8 radiant damage and being blinded for 1 minute on a failure, or half and not blinded on a success (blinded creatures re-save each turn); a creature ending its turn in the wall takes 4d8 radiant. As an action you can fire a beam from the wall at a creature within 60 feet of it, making a ranged spell attack for 4d8 radiant; each beam shortens the wall by 10 feet, and the spell ends when it reaches 0.
wall of light.higher: All damage increases by 1d8 per slot level above 5th.

wall of sand.name: Wall of Sand
wall of sand.summary: A wall of swirling sand 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 10 feet thick blocks sight. Creatures inside are blinded and move at a third of their speed.
wall of sand.text: You raise a wall of whirling sand up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 10 feet thick on the ground. It blocks line of sight but not movement. A creature inside the wall's space is blinded and must spend 3 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

wall of stone.name: Wall of Stone
wall of stone.summary: Raise a wall of ten 10-by-10-foot stone panels, 6 inches thick. If you hold concentration for the full duration, the wall becomes permanent.
wall of stone.text:
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into existence at a point you choose within range. The wall is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-footby-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.

If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side). If a creature would be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall and another solid surface), that creature can make a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no longer enclosed by the wall.

The wall can have any shape you desire, though it can't occupy the same space as a creature or object. The wall doesn't need to be vertical or rest on a firm foundation. It must, however, merge with and be solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.

If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length, you must halve the size of each panel to create supports. You can crudely shape the wall to create battlements and the like. The wall is an object made of stone that can be damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15 and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause connected panels to collapse at the GM's discretion.

If you maintain your Concentration on this spell for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent and can't be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disappears when the spell ends.

wall of thorns.name: Wall of Thorns
wall of thorns.summary: You create a wall of tough, pliable, tangled brush bristling with needle-sharp thorns.
wall of thorns.text:
You create a wall of tangled brush bristling with needle-sharp thorns. The wall appears within range on a solid surface and lasts for the duration. You choose to make the wall up to 60 feet long, 10 feet high, and 5 feet thick or a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. The wall blocks line of sight.

When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 7d8 Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

A creature can move through the wall, albeit slowly and painfully. For every 1 foot a creature moves through the wall, it must spend 4 feet of movement. Furthermore, the first time a creature enters a space in the wall on a turn or ends its turn there, the creature makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 7d8 Slashing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature makes this save only once per turn.
wall of thorns.higher: Both types of damage increase by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 6.

wall of water.name: Wall of Water
wall of water.summary: A wall of water is difficult terrain, hinders ranged weapon attacks through it, halves fire passing through, and freezes from cold.
wall of water.text: You create a wall of water up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high and 1 foot thick, or a ring up to 20 feet across and 20 feet high. Its space is difficult terrain, ranged weapon attacks passing through it have disadvantage, and fire effects passing through it deal half damage. Cold damage passing through freezes at least a 5-foot section solid (AC 5, 15 hit points), and a destroyed frozen section leaves a gap.

warding bond.name: Warding Bond
warding bond.material: a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear for the duration
warding bond.summary: A creature gains +1 AC and saves and resistance to all damage, but you take the same damage it does. Needs a pair of 50 gp platinum rings.
warding bond.text:
You touch another creature that is willing and create a mystic connection between you and the target until the spell ends. While the target is within 60 feet of you, it gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws, and it has Resistance to all damage. Also, each time it takes damage, you take the same amount of damage.

The spell ends if you drop to 0 Hit Points or if you and the target become separated by more than 60 feet. It also ends if the spell is cast again on either of the connected creatures.

warding wind.name: Warding Wind
warding wind.summary: A 10-ft gale around you deafens, snuffs small flames, blocks gas, is difficult terrain for others and hinders ranged attacks.
warding wind.text: A strong wind whirls in a 10-foot radius around you and moves with you. It deafens you and other creatures inside it, puts out unprotected flames the size of a torch or smaller, keeps out gas, vapor and fog, makes the area difficult terrain for creatures other than you, and gives disadvantage to ranged weapon attacks that pass into or out of it.

water breathing.name: Water Breathing
water breathing.summary: Up to ten willing creatures can breathe underwater for the duration. Can be cast as a ritual.
water breathing.text: This spell grants up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range the ability to breathe underwater until the spell ends. Affected creatures also retain their normal mode of respiration.

water walk.name: Water Walk
water walk.summary: Up to ten willing creatures can move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground. Can be cast as a ritual.
water walk.text:
This spell grants the ability to move across any liquid surface-such as water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, or lava-as if it were harmless solid ground (creatures crossing molten lava can still take damage from the heat). Up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range gain this ability for the duration.

An affected target must take a Bonus Action to pass from the liquid's surface into the liquid itself and vice versa, but if the target falls into the liquid, the target passes through the surface into the liquid below.

watery sphere.name: Watery Sphere
watery sphere.summary: A 5-foot-radius sphere of water traps up to four Medium creatures on failed Str saves, restraining them. Roll it 30 feet as an action.
watery sphere.text: A 5-foot-radius sphere of water appears at a point you can see; creatures in its area make a Strength save or are restrained and engulfed (it holds up to four Medium or smaller creatures or one Large creature; Huge or larger automatically succeed). A restrained creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. As an action you can roll the sphere up to 30 feet, carrying anyone trapped inside and forcing new saves on creatures it rams. When the spell ends, the sphere splashes down, putting out ordinary flames within 30 feet and leaving trapped creatures prone.

web.name: Web
web.summary: You conjure a mass of thick, sticky webbing at a point of your choice within range.
web.text:
You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point within range. The webs fill a 20-foot Cube there for the duration. The webs are Difficult Terrain, and the area within them is Lightly Obscured.

If the webs aren't anchored between two solid masses (such as walls or trees) or layered across a floor, wall, or ceiling, the web collapses on itself, and the spell ends at the start of your next turn. Webs layered over a flat surface have a depth of 5 feet.

The first time a creature enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Restrained condition while in the webs or until it breaks free.

A creature Restrained by the webs can take an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer Restrained.

The webs are flammable. Any 5-foot Cube of webs exposed to fire burns away in 1 round, dealing 2d4 Fire damage to any creature that starts its turn in the fire.

weird.name: Weird
weird.summary: Drawing on the deepest fears of a group of creatures, you create illusory creatures in their minds, visible only to them.
weird.text:
You try to create illusory terrors in others' minds. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 10d10 Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition for the duration. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

A Frightened target makes a Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it takes 5d10 Psychic damage. On a successful save, the spell ends on that target.

whirlwind.name: Whirlwind
whirlwind.summary: A 10-ft radius, 30-ft tall cyclone moves 30 ft per action: Dex save or 10d6 bludgeoning, and it can suck up and hold creatures.
whirlwind.text: A whirlwind 10 feet in radius and 30 feet tall forms at a point on the ground, and as an action you can move it up to 30 feet. A creature that enters it for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Dexterity save, taking 10d6 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success. A Large or smaller creature that fails must also make a Strength save or be restrained and lifted inside, rising 5 feet each turn and moving with the whirlwind. A trapped creature can use an action to escape with a Strength or Dexterity check against your DC, and is flung away in a random direction.

wind walk.name: Wind Walk
wind walk.summary: You and up to ten willing creatures you can see within range assume a gaseous form for the duration, appearing as wisps of cloud.
wind walk.text:
You and up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range assume gaseous forms for the duration, appearing as wisps of cloud. While in this cloud form, a target has a Fly Speed of 300 feet and can hover; it has Immunity to the Prone condition; and it has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage. The only actions a target can take in this form are the Dash action or a Magic action to begin reverting to its normal form. Reverting takes 1 minute, during which the target has the Stunned condition. Until the spell ends, the target can revert to cloud form, which also requires a Magic action followed by a 1-minute transformation.

If a target is in cloud form and flying when the effect ends, the target descends 60 feet per round for 1 minute until it lands, which it does safely. If it can't land after 1 minute, it falls the remaining distance.

wind wall.name: Wind Wall
wind wall.summary: A wall of strong wind rises from the ground at a point you choose within range.
wind wall.text:
A wall of strong wind rises from the ground at a point you choose within range. You can make the wall up to 50 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot thick. You can shape the wall in any way you choose so long as it makes one continuous path along the ground. The wall lasts for the duration.

When the wall appears, each creature in its area makes a Strength saving throw, taking 4d8 Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The strong wind keeps fog, smoke, and other gases at bay. Small or smaller flying creatures or objects can't pass through the wall. Loose, lightweight materials brought into the wall fly upward. Arrows, bolts, and other ordinary projectiles launched at targets behind the wall are deflected upward and miss automatically. Boulders hurled by Giants or siege engines, and similar projectiles, are unaffected. Creatures in gaseous form can't pass through it.

wish.name: Wish
wish.summary: Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal creature can cast.
wish.text:
Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal can cast. By simply speaking aloud, you can alter reality itself.

The basic use of this spell is to duplicate any other spell of level 8 or lower. If you use it this way, you don't need to meet any requirements to cast that spell, including costly components. The spell simply takes effect.

Alternatively, you can create one of the following effects of your choice: Object Creation. You create one object of up to 25,000 GP in value that isn't a magic item. The object can be no more than 300 feet in any dimension, and it appears in an unoccupied space that you can see on the ground. Instant Health. You allow yourself and up to twenty creatures that you can see to regain all Hit Points, and you end all effects on them listed in the Greater Restoration spell. Resistance. You grant up to ten creatures that you can see Resistance to one damage type that you choose. This Resistance is permanent. Spell Immunity. You grant up to ten creatures you can see immunity to a single spell or other magical effect for 8 hours. Sudden Learning. You replace one of your feats with another feat for which you are eligible. You lose all the benefits of the old feat and gain the benefits of the new one. You can't replace a feat that is a prerequisite for any of your other feats or features. Roll Redo. You undo a single recent event by forcing a reroll of any die roll made within the last round (including your last turn). Reality reshapes itself to accommodate the new result. For example, a Wish spell could undo an ally's failed saving throw or a foe's Critical Hit. You can force the reroll to be made with Advantage or Disadvantage, and you choose whether to use the reroll or the original roll. Reshape Reality. You may wish for something not included in any of the other effects. To do so, state your wish to the GM as precisely as possible. The GM has great latitude in ruling what occurs in such an instance; the greater the wish, the greater the likelihood that something goes wrong. This spell might simply fail, the effect you desire might be achieved only in part, or you might suffer an unforeseen consequence as a result of how you worded the wish. For example, wishing that a villain were dead might propel you forward in time to a period when that villain is no longer alive, effectively removing you from the game. Similarly, wishing for a Legendary magic item or an Artifact might instantly transport you to the presence of the item's current owner. If your wish is granted and its effects have consequences for a whole community, region, or world, you are likely to attract powerful foes. If your wish would affect a god, the god's divine servants might instantly intervene to prevent it or to encourage you to craft the wish in a particular way. If your wish would undo the multiverse itself, your wish fails. The stress of casting Wish to produce any effect other than duplicating another spell weakens you. After enduring that stress, each time you cast a spell until you finish a Long Rest, you take 1d10 Necrotic damage per level of that spell. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way. In addition, your Strength score becomes 3 for 2d4 days. For each of those days that you spend resting and doing nothing more than light activity, your remaining recovery time decreases by 2 days. Finally, there is a 33 percent chance that you are unable to cast Wish ever again if you suffer this stress.

witch bolt.name: Witch Bolt
witch bolt.material: a twig from a tree struck by lightning
witch bolt.summary: Ranged spell attack for 1d12 lightning. On later turns you can use your action to deal 1d12 lightning to it automatically while it stays in range.
witch bolt.text: A crackling beam leaps to a creature in range; make a ranged spell attack, dealing 1d12 lightning damage on a hit. On each of your later turns you can use your action to deal another 1d12 lightning damage to the target automatically. The spell ends if you use your action for anything else, or if the target moves out of range or gains total cover from you.
witch bolt.higher: The initial damage increases by 1d12 per slot level above 1st.

word of radiance.name: Word of Radiance
word of radiance.summary: Each creature you choose within 5 ft makes a Con save or takes 1d6 radiant.
word of radiance.text: You speak a holy word and searing light bursts from you. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 5 feet makes a Constitution save or takes 1d6 radiant damage.
word of radiance.higher: Damage rises by one die at 5th level (2d6), 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

word of recall.name: Word of Recall
word of recall.summary: You and up to five willing creatures within 5 feet of you instantly teleport to a previously designated sanctuary.
word of recall.text:
You and up to five willing creatures within 5 feet of you instantly teleport to a previously designated sanctuary. You and any creatures that teleport with you appear in the nearest unoccupied space to the spot you designated when you prepared your sanctuary (see below). If you cast this spell without first preparing a sanctuary, the spell has no effect.

You must designate a location, such as a temple, as a sanctuary by casting this spell there.

wrath of nature.name: Wrath of Nature
wrath of nature.summary: Animate the plants and rocks in a 60-ft cube: slowing undergrowth, lashing trees (4d6), grasping roots and hurled stones (3d8).
wrath of nature.text: Nature in a 60-foot cube rises against your foes. Grass and undergrowth become difficult terrain for your enemies. At the start of each of your turns, enemies within 10 feet of a tree in the cube make a Dexterity save or take 4d6 slashing damage. At the end of each of your turns, one creature you choose on the ground makes a Strength save or is restrained by roots until it escapes with a Strength (Athletics) check against your DC. As a bonus action, you can hurl a loose rock at a creature in the cube with a ranged spell attack for 3d8 bludgeoning, and the target makes a Strength save or falls prone.

wrathful smite.name: Wrathful Smite
wrathful smite.summary: Your next melee weapon hit deals an extra 1d6 psychic. Wis save or the target is frightened until it succeeds on a Wisdom check as an action.
wrathful smite.text: The next time you hit with a melee weapon attack during the duration, the attack deals an extra 1d6 psychic damage. If the target is a creature, it makes a Wisdom save or is frightened of you until the spell ends. The frightened creature can use its action to make a Wisdom check against your spell save DC to shake off the fear.

zephyr strike.name: Zephyr Strike
zephyr strike.summary: Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. Once, you can make a weapon attack with advantage for an extra 1d8 force on a hit and +30 feet of speed.
zephyr strike.text: You move like the wind: your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks until the spell ends. Once during the duration you can give yourself advantage on one weapon attack roll on your turn; that attack deals an extra 1d8 force damage on a hit, and hit or miss your walking speed increases by 30 feet until the end of that turn. The spell then ends.

zone of truth.name: Zone of Truth
zone of truth.summary: Creatures in a 15-foot-radius sphere make a Cha save or can't knowingly lie there. You know who failed.
zone of truth.text:
You create a magical zone that guards against deception in a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range. Until the spell ends, a creature that enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can't speak a deliberate lie while in the radius. You know whether a creature succeeds or fails on this save.

An affected creature is aware of the spell and can avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive yet must be truthful.
